Surah 93 is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1–3} Allah swears by the day when its brightness spreads, by the forenoon, and by the night when it becomes still and its darkness settles, to show Allah's care for His Messenger (ﷺ). He says: {Your Lord has not forsaken you} — that is, He has not abandoned you since He took care of you, nor neglected you since He raised and nurtured you; rather, He has never ceased to bring you up in the most perfect manner and to elevate you degree after degree. {Nor has He detested you} — that is, He has not hated you since He loved you. The negation of an opposite is evidence of the affirmation of its opposite, and pure negation is not praiseworthy unless it implies the affirmation of a perfection. So this is the Messenger's (ﷺ) past and present state, the most complete and perfect state: Allah's love for him, its continuation, His elevating him in degrees of perfection, and the enduring of Allah's care for him.

{4} As for his future state, He says: {And the Hereafter is better for you than the present} — that is, every later state of yours is superior to the state before it. The Messenger (ﷺ) continued to ascend the degrees of excellence; Allah established his religion for him, gave him victory over his enemies, and guided him aright in his affairs, until he died having attained a station that neither the first nor the last had reached, in virtues, blessings, comfort of the eye and gladness of heart.

{5} After this, do not ask about his state in the Hereafter, with its details of honour and kinds of bounty. For this reason He says: {And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied}. This is a matter that can be expressed only by this comprehensive and all-encompassing phrase.

{6–8} Then He bestowed favour upon him by mentioning what He knew of his particular circumstances, saying: {Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?} — that is, He found you without mother or father; both your father and mother had died while you could not manage your own affairs, so Allah sheltered you. Your grandfather ʿAbd al-Muttalib took charge of you, and when your grandfather died, Allah placed you under the guardianship of your uncle Abu Talib, until He strengthened you with His help and with the believers. {And He found you lost and guided you} — that is, He found you not knowing what the Book or faith was, so He taught you what you did not know and granted you success in the best deeds and character. {And He found you poor and made you self-sufficient} — that is, poor, so He enriched you through the lands He opened for you, whose wealth and tribute were collected for you. He who removed these deficiencies from you will remove every other deficiency, and He who brought you to wealth, sheltered you, gave you victory and guided you, so respond to His blessing with gratitude.

{9–11} For this reason He says: {So as for the orphan, do not oppress him}, that is, do not mistreat the orphan, do not let your heart be constricted toward him, do not scold him; rather, honour him, give him what is within your means, and treat him as you would wish your own child to be treated after you. {And as for the petitioner, do not repel him}, that is, let no word issue from you to a petitioner that would turn him away from his request through harshness and roughness of character; rather, give him what you can, or turn him away with kindness and goodness. This includes the one who seeks wealth and the one who seeks knowledge. For this reason the teacher is commanded to have good character with the student, to deal with him generously and with compassion, for in that is help for him in attaining his aim and honour for one who strives to benefit the servants and the lands. {And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it}. This includes religious and worldly blessings; that is, praise Allah for them, single them out for mention if there is a benefit in doing so, and otherwise speak of the blessings of Allah in general, for speaking of Allah's blessing calls to thanking Him and makes hearts beloved of the one who bestowed it, since hearts are naturally inclined to love the benefactor.

So this is the Messenger's (ﷺ) past and present state, the most complete and perfect state: Allah's love for him, its continuation, His elevating him in degrees of perfection, and the enduring of Allah's care for him.

{4} As for his future state, He says: {And the Hereafter is better for you than the present} — that is, every later state of yours is superior to the state before it. The Messenger (ﷺ) continued to ascend the degrees of excellence; Allah established his religion for him, gave him victory over his enemies, and guided him aright in his affairs, until he died having attained a station that neither the first nor the last had reached, in virtues, blessings, comfort of the eye and gladness of heart.

{5} After this, do not ask about his state in the Hereafter, with its details of honour and kinds of bounty. For this reason He says: {And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied}. This is a matter that can be expressed only by this comprehensive and all-encompassing phrase.

{6–8} Then He bestowed favour upon him by mentioning what He knew of his particular circumstances, saying: {Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?} — that is, He found you without mother or father; both your father and mother had died while you could not manage your own affairs, so Allah sheltered you. Your grandfather ʿAbd al-Muttalib took charge of you, and when your grandfather died, Allah placed you under the guardianship of your uncle Abu Talib, until He strengthened you with His help and with the believers. {And He found you lost and guided you} — that is, He found you not knowing what the Book or faith was, so He taught you what you did not know and granted you success in the best deeds and character. {And He found you poor and made you self-sufficient} — that is, poor, so He enriched you through the lands He opened for you, whose wealth and tribute were collected for you. He who removed these deficiencies from you will remove every other deficiency, and He who brought you to wealth, sheltered you, gave you victory and guided you, so respond to His blessing with gratitude.

{9–11} For this reason He says: {So as for the orphan, do not oppress him}, that is, do not mistreat the orphan, do not let your heart be constricted toward him, do not scold him; rather, honour him, give him what is within your means, and treat him as you would wish your own child to be treated after you. {And as for the petitioner, do not repel him}, that is, let no word issue from you to a petitioner that would turn him away from his request through harshness and roughness of character; rather, give him what you can, or turn him away with kindness and goodness. This includes the one who seeks wealth and the one who seeks knowledge. For this reason the teacher is commanded to have good character with the student, to deal with him generously and with compassion, for in that is help for him in attaining his aim and honour for one who strives to benefit the servants and the lands. {And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it}. This includes religious and worldly blessings; that is, praise Allah for them, single them out for mention if there is a benefit in doing so, and otherwise speak of the blessings of Allah in general, for speaking of Allah's blessing calls to thanking Him and makes hearts beloved of the one who bestowed it, since hearts are naturally inclined to love the benefactor.
